Timestral-209M · saved forecast replay

Lower confidence gates, more trades.
Same market data and probabilities.

The primary lower-threshold rule executes 597 of the same 1,800 opportunities, compared with 1 previously. It skips 1,203 and uses 2× or 3× exposure on 213 trades.

First: what confidence measures

Confidence is the estimated probability that a proposed next-bar trade makes money after fees, financing and short borrow. It is not the probability that the price simply moves in the predicted direction, and it is not a measure of expected return. The model’s median forecast still chooses long or short.

The existing calculation turns the model’s 21 next-price quantiles into an approximate probability of crossing the trade’s break-even price. That price includes costs at each of 1×, 2× and 3×. A monotone regularized sigmoid, fitted separately for each instrument and timeframe using 300 earlier forecast origins, calibrates those probabilities. There is a one-bar embargo before each later 200-opportunity sample. The calibration map is frozen and clamps inputs to the calibration range. This replay reuses those saved probabilities exactly.

Previously, the gates were 55% / 60% / 70%. Now they are 35% / 40% / 45%. Choose the highest exposure whose own probability clears its gate; otherwise hold cash. A flat median forecast always skips. For example, probabilities 43% / 42% / 41% select 2× under the primary rule, while 48% / 47% / 46% select 3×. Each number is the probability for that exposure level’s costs.

A 40% estimated win probability means roughly 4 profitable trades out of 10 if the estimate is accurate. Lowering a gate does not improve confidence. Win rate alone does not determine profit; win and loss sizes also matter. The earlier probability audit beat raw Brier scores in 4/9 cases and a constant historical probability in 6/9 cases.

The result of relaxing the gates

The primary rule has 0 profitable, 3 loss-making and 6 unchanged accounts. It produces a lower net return than the original rule in 3/9 accounts. Additional executions are not evidence of a better strategy; read the account returns alongside the increased trade count.

Each account starts with 100,000: INR for Reliance, USD for SPY and EUR/USD. Accounts remain separate; INR and USD P&L are not added together.

Why some minute cases still skip

The saved calibrated profit probabilities are very low on minute data because round-trip fees often exceed the next-bar movement. Lowering a confidence gate does not remove those costs. The schedules above accept only probabilities at or above their stated gates; the unfiltered 1× comparator shows what happens if all non-flat model signals are traded anyway.

Execution assumptions and reproducibility

The Yahoo Finance snapshot, Timestral revision, 250-close contexts, forecast medians, directions, calibration parameters, probabilities, entry/exit timestamps and holding periods are identical to the preceding confidence report. No model inference, calibration refit or new download was needed.

  • 200 opportunities per case: Reliance, SPY and EUR/USD × minute, hourly and daily bars.
  • Ideal observed-close to next-observed-close fills, including overnight/weekend gaps. Same-close signal execution excludes latency.
  • Fees per entry and exit: Reliance 10 basis points, SPY 5, EUR/USD 2. These are unchanged simulation assumptions.
  • 8% annual financing on exposure above 1×; 3% annual short borrow; elapsed calendar time, including weekends. No FX carry, taxes, separate exchange fees or margin-call/intrabar liquidation simulation.
  • Effective starting exposure = requested leverage / (1 + per-fill cost × requested leverage), leaving the entry fee in the account. Exposure labels 1×/2×/3× refer to requested leverage.
  • Daily inputs use retrospective adjusted closes; model training overlap is unknown. No broker orders are placed.
